description: Transvaalbuurt-West 1922-23 portiek blocks (Albert Luthulistraat 25-27 and 33-35): the same four-storey dark red-brown brick front as the tower blocks, one big white three-light window either side of a narrow stair axis whose windows stand between header-course brick ladders, the portiek door under a flat concrete canopy at its foot; over the stair axis the parapet rises about 1.8 m in a short raised panel; the dark glazed-brick parapet band with dentils runs the row

match.note: the stair-axis pands without a tower (BAG 1922-23, 3DBAG eaves 12.2 m); the strip skyline reads the setback fifth storey or the raised stair panel (13.3-13.7 m). No roof criterion: the setback fifth storey behind the parapet reads as a 3.0-3.6 m roof rise on 3DBAG. The two types are told apart by that skyline (frontSkylineM). Frontage: BAG cuts the 1921-1923 portiek rows into stair blocks of 5.2-12.4 m (Albert Luthulistraat 21-41: 5.2-5.7 m stair pands beside 9.2-12.4 m window pands; Schalk Burgerstraat 2-140 5.2-10 m) for one front, so the house width is no veto; four storeys at the type pitch and a 1.6-6.5 m window-axis pitch (3 axes over 5.6-12.4 m) are. A 0.8 m pitch (Retiefstraat 220: 12 columns over 9.4 m) is a plain window grid, not this front

raised.note: Albert Luthulistraat 33-35 (126814): the raised stair panel 3.45-6.45 m from the pand's left, top 13.65 m (1.85 m = 0.65 upper storeys over the 11.8 m wall top)

door-centre.note: the portiek door on the stair axis under a flat concrete canopy (2.65-3.15 m, about 3.5 m wide); mailboxes either side

rhythm.bays: a window bay, the narrow stair axis, a window bay
rhythm.identicalBays: no: the stair axis is narrow
rhythm.windowsPerStorey: ground: window + portiek door + window | 1-3: window + stair window + window
rhythm.groundFloor: one portiek door under a flat concrete canopy, two windows
rhythm.roofline: flat, a dark brick parapet band with dentils, a short raised panel over the stair axis

evidence.citation: strip.jpg 2020-04-29 at 40 px/m, pavement at y 638 px: 126814 (10.8 m) windows 0.6-2.7 and 7.2-9.1 m; stair windows 4.6-5.4 m between brick ladders; raised panel 3.45-6.45 m to 13.65 m; sills/heads and wall top as the tower type. 105200 (10.9 m, BAG 1949 rebuild of the same front) the same

the header-course brick ladders either side of the stair windows (a lighter orange brick) are not drawn
the stair windows sit half a storey above the main windows' line and carry a transom; drawn as plain single lights on the main head line
the raised stair panel's own dentil frieze
